suggestions: convert aggregate functions into CASE expressions with division
restructure subquery with EXISTS for filtering
use derived table for aggregated data
pre-filter a large table as a CTE before the join
use a CTE to select top items first
join top items with filtered data
use CTEs to materialize filtered dimensions
split final result into top items CTE and main join
optimized_sql:
SELECT i.i_item_id,
       CASE WHEN SUM(fs.cnt_q) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(fs.sum_q)::numeric / SUM(fs.cnt_q) END AS agg1,
       CASE WHEN SUM(fs.cnt_lp) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(fs.sum_lp)::numeric / SUM(fs.cnt_lp) END AS agg2,
       CASE WHEN SUM(fs.cnt_ca) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(fs.sum_ca)::numeric / SUM(fs.cnt_ca) END AS agg3,
       CASE WHEN SUM(fs.cnt_sp) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(fs.sum_sp)::numeric / SUM(fs.cnt_sp) END AS agg4
FROM (
    SELECT ss.ss_item_sk,
           COUNT(ss.ss_quantity) AS cnt_q,
           SUM(ss.ss_quantity) AS sum_q,
           COUNT(ss.ss_list_price) AS cnt_lp,
           SUM(ss.ss_list_price) AS sum_lp,
           COUNT(ss.ss_coupon_amt) AS cnt_ca,
           SUM(ss.ss_coupon_amt) AS sum_ca,
           COUNT(ss.ss_sales_price) AS cnt_sp,
           SUM(ss.ss_sales_price) AS sum_sp
    FROM store_sales ss
    WHERE EXISTS (
            SELECT cd.cd_demo_sk
            FROM customer_demographics cd
            WHERE cd.cd_demo_sk = ss.ss_cdemo_sk
              AND cd.cd_gender = 'F'
              AND cd.cd_marital_status = 'W'
              AND cd.cd_education_status = 'College'
          )
      AND EXISTS (
            SELECT dd.d_date_sk
            FROM date_dim dd
            WHERE dd.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
              AND dd.d_year = 2001
          )
      AND EXISTS (
            SELECT p.p_promo_sk
            FROM promotion p
            WHERE p.p_promo_sk = ss.ss_promo_sk
              AND (p.p_channel_email = 'N' OR p.p_channel_event = 'N')
          )
    GROUP BY ss.ss_item_sk
) AS fs
JOIN item i ON fs.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
GROUP BY i.i_item_id
ORDER BY i.i_item_id
LIMIT 100

reasoning_trace:
1. BITMAP FACT-FILTER — TARGET: store_sales.ss_cdemo_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_promo_sk — TRANSFORMATION: Create single-column btree indexes on those three fact FK columns and bitmap-intersect the filtered dimension key sets (female/widowed/College customer_demographics, d_year=2001 date_dim, promotion OR-condition) before any join or aggregation, so the 57.6M-row store_sales scan is reduced to only the rows that can survive the dimension filters.

2. EXISTENCE-PREDICATE REWRITE — TARGET: the three inner joins to customer_demographics, date_dim, and promotion — TRANSFORMATION: Rewrite those dimension joins as correlated existence predicates on the fact FK columns with the selective dimension filters inside, making it explicit that customer_demographics/date_dim/promotion are filters on store_sales, not row-multiplying joins, and allowing the planner to apply them before the item join/grouping.

3. TWO-PHASE AGGREGATION — TARGET: store_sales.ss_item_sk → item.i_item_id — TRANSFORMATION: First group the filtered store_sales rows by ss_item_sk and carry SUM/COUNT for ss_quantity, ss_list_price, ss_coupon_amt, and ss_sales_price; then join item on i_item_sk and group by i_item_id using weighted AVG values, so the final GROUP BY/ORDER BY/LIMIT operates on at most one row per item_sk instead of on the full qualified fact row set.
